import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"

func TestGmetaStore_WriteCommitted_SingleSession(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	repo := initTestRepo(t)
	store := NewGmetaStore(repo)
	ctx := context.Background()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a3b2c4d5e6f7")

	err := store.WriteCommitted(ctx, WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID:     cpID,
		SessionID:        "session-001",
		Strategy:         "manual-commit",
		Branch:           "main",
		Transcript:       []byte(`{"type":"text","content":"hello"}`),
		Prompts:          []string{"build a feature"},
		FilesTouched:     []string{"src/foo.go", "src/bar.go"},
		CheckpointsCount: 3,
		AuthorName:       "Test",
		AuthorEmail:      "test@test.com",
		Agent:            agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		Model:            "claude-opus-4-6",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify ref exists
	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(GmetaRefName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the tree and verify structure
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify the target path exists: change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
	targetPath := gmetaTargetPath(cpID)
	targetTree, err := tree.Tree(targetPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Flatten and check entries
	entries := make(map[string]string)
	flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, targetTree, "", entries)

	// Check checkpoint-level fields
	assert.Equal(t, "manual-commit", entries["entire/strategy/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "main", entries["entire/branch/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "3", entries["entire/checkpoints-count/__value"])
	assert.NotEmpty(t, entries["entire/cli-version/__value"])

	// Check files-touched set entries exist (2 files)
	setCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "entire/files-touched/__set/") {
			setCount++

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface {
	BlobObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error)
	TreeObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error)
}, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			if _, readErr := reader.Read(content); readErr != nil {
				_ = reader.Close()
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read content at %s: %v", path, readErr)
				continue
			}
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

func TestGmetaStore_WriteCommitted_SingleSession(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	repo := initTestRepo(t)
	store := NewGmetaStore(repo)
	ctx := context.Background()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a3b2c4d5e6f7")

	err := store.WriteCommitted(ctx, WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID:     cpID,
		SessionID:        "session-001",
		Strategy:         "manual-commit",
		Branch:           "main",
		Transcript:       redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte(`{"type":"text","content":"hello"}`)),
		Prompts:          []string{"build a feature"},
		FilesTouched:     []string{"src/foo.go", "src/bar.go"},
		CheckpointsCount: 3,
		AuthorName:       "Test",
		AuthorEmail:      "test@test.com",
		Agent:            agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		Model:            "claude-opus-4-6",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify ref exists
	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(GmetaRefName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the tree and verify structure
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify the target path exists: change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
	targetPath := gmetaTargetPath(cpID)
	targetTree, err := tree.Tree(targetPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Flatten and check entries
	entries := make(map[string]string)
	flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, targetTree, "", entries)

	// Check checkpoint-level fields
	assert.Equal(t, "manual-commit", entries["entire/strategy/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "main", entries["entire/branch/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "3", entries["entire/checkpoints-count/__value"])
	assert.NotEmpty(t, entries["entire/cli-version/__value"])

	// Check files-touched set entries exist (2 files)
	setCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "entire/files-touched/__set/") {
			setCount++
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 2, setCount, "expected 2 files-touched set entries")

	// Check session agent info
	assert.Equal(t, string(agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode), entries["session/session-001/agent/name/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "claude-opus-4-6", entries["session/session-001/agent/model/__value"])

	// Check prompt
	assert.Equal(t, "build a feature", entries["session/session-001/prompt/__value"])

	// Check transcript list has entries
	transcriptCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "session/session-001/transcript/__list/") {
			transcriptCount++
		}
	}
	assert.Positive(t, transcriptCount, "expected transcript list entries")

	// Check session IDs list
	idsCount := 0
	for key, val := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "session/ids/__list/") {
			idsCount++
			assert.Equal(t, "session-001", val)
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 1, idsCount, "expected 1 session ID list entry")
}

func TestGmetaStore_WriteCommitted_IncrementalTask(t *testing.T) {

		IsTask:              true,
		ToolUseID:           "toolu_abc123",
		IsIncremental:       true,
		IncrementalSequence: 1,
		IncrementalType:     "write_file",
		IncrementalData:     []byte(`{"file":"test.go","content":"package main"}`),
		AuthorName:          "Test",
		AuthorEmail:         "test@test.com",
		Agent:               agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read back and verify incremental list entry

	require.NoError(t, err)

	for key := range entries {

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface {
	BlobObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error)
	TreeObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error)
}, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			if _, readErr := reader.Read(content); readErr != nil {
				_ = reader.Close()
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read content at %s: %v", path, readErr)
				continue
			}
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface {
	BlobObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error)
	TreeObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error)
}, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			if _, readErr := reader.Read(content); readErr != nil {
				_ = reader.Close()
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read content at %s: %v", path, readErr)
				continue
			}
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

func TestGmetaStore_WriteCommitted_SingleSession(t *testing.T) {

	repo := initTestRepo(t)
	store := NewGmetaStore(repo)
	ctx := context.Background()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("a3b2c4d5e6f7")

	err := store.WriteCommitted(ctx, WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID:     cpID,
		SessionID:        "session-001",
		Strategy:         "manual-commit",
		Branch:           "main",
		Transcript:       redact.AlreadyRedacted([]byte(`{"type":"text","content":"hello"}`)),
		Prompts:          []string{"build a feature"},
		FilesTouched:     []string{"src/foo.go", "src/bar.go"},
		CheckpointsCount: 3,
		AuthorName:       "Test",
		AuthorEmail:      "test@test.com",
		Agent:            agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		Model:            "claude-opus-4-6",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify ref exists
	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(GmetaRefName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the tree and verify structure
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify the target path exists: change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
	targetPath := gmetaTargetPath(cpID)
	targetTree, err := tree.Tree(targetPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Flatten and check entries
	entries := make(map[string]string)
	flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, targetTree, "", entries)

	// Check checkpoint-level fields
	assert.Equal(t, "manual-commit", entries["entire/strategy/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "main", entries["entire/branch/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "3", entries["entire/checkpoints-count/__value"])
	assert.NotEmpty(t, entries["entire/cli-version/__value"])

	// Check files-touched set entries exist (2 files)
	setCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "entire/files-touched/__set/") {
			setCount++
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 2, setCount, "expected 2 files-touched set entries")

	// Check session agent info
	assert.Equal(t, string(agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode), entries["session/session-001/agent/name/__value"])
	assert.Equal(t, "claude-opus-4-6", entries["session/session-001/agent/model/__value"])

	// Check prompt
	assert.Equal(t, "build a feature", entries["session/session-001/prompt/__value"])

	// Check transcript list has entries
	transcriptCount := 0
	for key := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "session/session-001/transcript/__list/") {
			transcriptCount++
		}
	}
	assert.Positive(t, transcriptCount, "expected transcript list entries")

	// Check session IDs list
	idsCount := 0
	for key, val := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(key, "session/ids/__list/") {
			idsCount++
			assert.Equal(t, "session-001", val)
		}
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 1, idsCount, "expected 1 session ID list entry")
}

// flattenTreeToStrings recursively flattens a tree into a map of path -> blob content.
func flattenTreeToStrings(t *testing.T, repo interface {
	BlobObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Blob, error)
	TreeObject(hash plumbing.Hash) (*object.Tree, error)
}, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, out map[string]string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
		path := entry.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			path = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
		}

		if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
			blob, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read blob at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			reader, err := blob.Reader()
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to get reader at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			content := make([]byte, blob.Size)
			if _, readErr := reader.Read(content); readErr != nil {
				_ = reader.Close()
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read content at %s: %v", path, readErr)
				continue
			}
			_ = reader.Close()
			out[path] = string(content)
		} else {
			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
			if err != nil {
				t.Logf("warning: failed to read subtree at %s: %v", path, err)
				continue
			}
			flattenTreeToStrings(t, repo, subtree, path, out)
		}
	}
}

func TestMigrateCheckpointsV2_UsesComputedCompactTranscriptStart(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	repo := initMigrateTestRepo(t)

	ctx := context.Background()

	cpID := id.MustCheckpointID("5566778899aa")
	transcript := []byte(
		"{\"type\":\"human\",\"message\":{\"content\":\"prompt 1\"}}\n" +
			"{\"type\":\"assistant\",\"message\":{\"content\":\"reply 1\"}}\n" +
			"{\"type\":\"human\",\"message\":{\"content\":\"prompt 2\"}}\n" +
			"{\"type\":\"assistant\",\"message\":{\"content\":\"reply 2\"}}\n",
	)
	err := v1Store.WriteCommitted(ctx, checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions{
		CheckpointID:              cpID,
		SessionID:                 "session-compact-start-migrate",
		Strategy:                  "manual-commit",
		Transcript:                redact.AlreadyRedacted(transcript),
		Prompts:                   []string{"prompt 2"},
		Agent:                     agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		CheckpointTranscriptStart: 2, // full transcript line domain
		AuthorName:                "Test",
		AuthorEmail:               "test@test.com",
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	v1Content, err := v1Store.ReadSessionContent(ctx, cpID, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	fullCompacted := tryCompactTranscript(ctx, v1Content.Transcript, v1Content.Metadata)
	require.NotNil(t, fullCompacted)
	scopedCompacted, err := compact.Compact(redact.AlreadyRedacted(v1Content.Transcript), compact.MetadataFields{
		Agent:      string(v1Content.Metadata.Agent),
		CLIVersion: versioninfo.Version,
		StartLine:  v1Content.Metadata.GetTranscriptStart(),
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, scopedCompacted)
	require.Greater(t, bytes.Count(fullCompacted, []byte{'\n'}), bytes.Count(scopedCompacted, []byte{'\n'}))
	expectedOffset := computeCompactOffset(ctx, v1Content.Transcript, fullCompacted, v1Content.Metadata)
	require.Positive(t, expectedOffset, "expected non-zero compact transcript start")

	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	result, migrateErr := migrateCheckpointsV2(ctx, repo, v1Store, v2Store, nil, &stdout, false)
	require.NoError(t, migrateErr)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, result.migrated)

	v2MainCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(v2MainRef.Hash())

	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, err)
	metadataContent, err := metadataFile.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var metadata checkpoint.CommittedMetadata
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(metadataContent), &metadata))
	assert.Equal(t, expectedOffset, metadata.CheckpointTranscriptStart)

	storedCompact, err := v2Store.ReadSessionCompactTranscript(ctx, cpID, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, fullCompacted, storedCompact, "migration should persist cumulative compact transcript")
}

| Read Path | Location | Status | Details |

The gmeta spec defines two refs:

- **`refs/meta/local/main`** — your local metadata (what we write to now)
- **`refs/meta/remotes/main`** — metadata received from others

When you `git push`, Entire's pre-push hook already piggybacks extra refs alongside the user's push. Today it pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` and optionally v2 refs. The question is whether to also push `refs/meta/local/main` in that same hook.

**Why you'd want it:** Without it, gmeta data stays local-only. Nobody else can `gmeta get` your checkpoint metadata from the remote. The whole point of the exchange format is that it's exchangeable — pushing it makes interop real rather than theoretical.

**Why it's not urgent for the POC:** The POC goal is proving we can write data that the Rust `gmeta` CLI reads back correctly — that's local validation. Push/fetch adds complexity (refspec configuration, remote ref naming conventions, interaction with `refs/meta/remotes/main` materialization) that's orthogonal to proving the format works.

**Practical consideration:** The existing pre-push hook pushes refs conditionally behind feature flags. Adding gmeta would follow the same pattern — gate behind `IsGmetaEnabled`, push `refs/meta/local/main` alongside the user's push. Maybe 10-15 lines of code. But the fetch/materialization side (what happens when someone else pulls your metadata) is a bigger design question that the gmeta spec's materialization doc covers.

**My recommendation:** Skip it for now, do it when you want to test actual multi-user exchange. The POC validates format correctness locally.

- **`refs/meta/remotes/main`** — metadata received from others

When you `git push`, Entire's pre-push hook already piggybacks extra refs alongside the user's push. Today it pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` and optionally v2 refs. The question is whether to also push `refs/meta/local/main` in that same hook.

**Why you'd want it:** Without it, gmeta data stays local-only. Nobody else can `gmeta get` your checkpoint metadata from the remote. The whole point of the exchange format is that it's exchangeable — pushing it makes interop real rather than theoretical.

**Why it's not urgent for the POC:** The POC goal is proving we can write data that the Rust `gmeta` CLI reads back correctly — that's local validation. Push/fetch adds complexity (refspec configuration, remote ref naming conventions, interaction with `refs/meta/remotes/main` materialization) that's orthogonal to proving the format works.

**Practical consideration:** The existing pre-push hook pushes refs conditionally behind feature flags. Adding gmeta would follow the same pattern — gate behind `IsGmetaEnabled`, push `refs/meta/local/main` alongside the user's push. Maybe 10-15 lines of code. But the fetch/materialization side (what happens when someone else pulls your metadata) is a bigger design question that the gmeta spec's materialization doc covers.

**My recommendation:** Skip it for now, do it when you want to test actual multi-user exchange. The POC validates format correctness locally.

- keep gmeta as an additional exchange format

- don’t read from gmeta by default outside the targeted fallback/read paths until feature parity is complete

- write path: unchanged, dual-write to v1/v2/gmeta as configured
- push path: continue pushing v2 refs and gmeta ref separately
- fetch path: do not try to merge gmeta into v2 or vice versa
- read path: prefer v2/v1, use gmeta only where explicitly wired or when the native format is absent

The next concrete work item under this topic is to document that policy and make the settings explicit, for example:
- `checkpoints_v2=true` controls v2

Here's what I found from walking through all 18 checkpoint conversations:

## Issues Found During Implementation

### 1. Task checkpoint serialization was wrong (fixed in `20a5b2cbdeb5`)
Incremental task checkpoints were writing only the raw payload instead of the full JSON envelope (`type`, `tool_use_id`, `timestamp`, `data`). Caught during a code review session.

### 2. Session ordering was non-deterministic (fixed in `20a5b2cbdeb5`)
The "latest session" was inferred from lexicographic filename order of gmeta list entries, which doesn't correspond to insertion order. Fixed to use the monotonic timestamp prefix in list entry IDs to reconstruct append order.

### 3. Rust gmeta CLI interop issues (fixed in `150fc1933f69`)
- The Rust `gmeta` CLI didn't have `gmeta init` as expected — test had to be adapted
- Required `gmeta remote add` + remote `refs/meta/main` for materialization to work
- Commit subjects had to match the Rust serializer pattern for materialization to ingest them
- Entry naming needed to be Rust-compatible

### 4. Combined attribution was missing from gmeta (fixed in `c7a76f54f560`)
Session-scoped attribution was written, but checkpoint-level `CombinedAttribution` was completely absent. The post-commit hook now dual-writes it.

### 5. Migration only works as v2 side effect, not standalone (fixed in `ba2e77f6daf4`)
Originally there was no `entire migrate --checkpoints gmeta` — gmeta migration only happened as a side effect of `--checkpoints v2` with `gmeta=true`. A dedicated migration mode was added.

### 6. Migration doesn't carry over checkpoint-level combined attribution (open)
The migrate path calls `WriteCommitted` for session data but does **not** call `UpdateCheckpointSummary`, so combined attribution is lost during migration.

## Questions Raised / Design Decisions Made

### Push/fetch coexistence policy (documented in `c7d9d836f4f9`)
- Decision: keep v2 as authoritative, gmeta as additional exchange format
- Push both when enabled, but never let gmeta failure block v1/v2
- Don't read from gmeta by default; prefer v2/v1
- Fetch/materialization deferred entirely

### Task checkpoint key policy (documented in `c7d9d836f4f9`)
- Decision: task keys under `session:<id>:task:<tool-use-id>:...` are Entire-specific opaque data
- Generic gmeta tooling only needs to preserve/expose them; Entire owns semantics

### Token usage schema (decided in `933450f6500c`)
- Store as individual gmeta keys under `session/<id>/entire/token-usage/{input,output,cache-read,...}/__value` rather than a single JSON blob
- Keeps partial lookups fast via gmeta native queries

## Still Open
- **Migration doesn't migrate combined attribution** — noted in conversation but not fixed
- **Read-side integration** — only resume uses gmeta; session list/show/explain don't
- **Fetch not implemented** — push works, no pull-side logic
- **`Transcript` type changed to `RedactedBytes`** — the rebase exposed this; all gmeta code was using raw `[]byte` (fixed in our session today)

1	# gmeta POC Plan
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	gmeta is a proposed standard for attaching arbitrary metadata to Git projects, designed by Scott Chacon (GitButler). It defines a tree layout spec for serializing `(target, key, value)` tuples into Git trees on `refs/meta/local/main`, exchangeable over standard Git protocol.
6	
7	Entire's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer is functionally equivalent to jj's `change-id` — a stable identifier embedded in the commit message that survives rebase/cherry-pick. This maps directly to gmeta's `change-id` target type, meaning checkpoint metadata keyed to `change-id:<checkpoint-id>` survives rewrites without any additional tooling.
8	
9	Reference implementation: `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta`
10	Spec: `gmeta/spec/README.md`
11	
12	## Goal
13	
14	Write Entire checkpoint metadata in gmeta exchange format alongside v1/v2, proving interop by reading it back with the Rust `gmeta` CLI.
15	
16	## Coexistence Policy
17	
18	For the current rollout, `v2` and `gmeta` are allowed to coexist, but only as
19	an explicit opt-in via separate settings. There is no implicit dependency
20	between them.
21	
22	- `strategy_options.checkpoints_v2 = true` enables v2 write/read/push behavior
23	- `strategy_options.gmeta = true` enables gmeta write/push behavior
24	- If both are true, parallel behavior is intentional and temporary
25	- `gmeta` does not require `checkpoints_v2`, and `checkpoints_v2` does not
26	  require `gmeta`
27	- Read precedence remains unchanged unless a future explicit setting is added
28	  (for example, `prefer_gmeta_reads`)
29	
30	Operationally:
31	- `v2` remains the primary Entire-native storage format
32	- `gmeta` is an exchange/interoperability format written and pushed separately
33	- gmeta fetch/materialize is independent of v2 fetch logic
34	- gmeta failures must remain non-fatal to the v1/v2 checkpoint flow
35	- Current fallback reads from `gmeta` are compatibility behavior, not backend
36	  selection policy. They exist to keep resume/log lookup working while the
37	  rollout is in progress and should not be treated as a stable precedence model.
38	
39	## Architecture
40	
41	No go-git changes needed. gmeta is just a tree layout convention — Entire already has all the plumbing:
42	- `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit` in `checkpoint/`
43	- `V2GitStore` as prior art for a second store struct composing `GitStore`
44	- Dual-write pattern already exists in `manual_commit_condensation.go`
45	
46	## Tree Layout Mapping
47	
48	### Fanout Rule
49	
50	Per gmeta spec (`spec/exchange-format/exchange.md`), `change-id` targets use: **first 2 hex chars of SHA-1(target-value)**.
51	
52	So for checkpoint ID `a3b2c4d5e6f7`: fanout = `sha1("a3b2c4d5e6f7")[:2]`.
53	
54	This is NOT the same as `checkpoint-id[:2]`. The fanout is derived from a hash of the value, not the value itself.
55	
56	### Per-Session Encoding
57	
58	A checkpoint can contain multiple sessions (concurrent agents, `entire attach`). gmeta has no native session concept, so we namespace per session under the checkpoint's change-id target:
59	
60	```
61	change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
62	├── entire/
63	│   ├── strategy/__value                           # "manual-commit"
64	│   ├── cli-version/__value                        # CLI version
65	│   ├── branch/__value                             # branch name
66	│   ├── checkpoints-count/__value                  # total across all sessions
67	│   ├── combined-attribution/
68	│   │   ├── calculated-at/__value
69	│   │   ├── agent-lines/__value
70	│   │   ├── agent-removed/__value
71	│   │   ├── human-added/__value
72	│   │   ├── human-modified/__value
73	│   │   ├── human-removed/__value
74	│   │   ├── total-committed/__value
75	│   │   ├── total-lines-changed/__value
76	│   │   ├── agent-percentage/__value
77	│   │   └── metric-version/__value
78	│   └── files-touched/__set/                       # merged from all sessions
79	│       ├── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/foo.go"
80	│       └── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/bar.go"
81	├── session/
82	│   ├── ids/__list/                                # ordered session IDs
83	│   │   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid1"
84	│   │   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid2"
85	│   ├── <session-id-1>/
86	│   │   ├── agent/
87	│   │   │   ├── name/__value                       # "Claude Code"
88	│   │   │   ├── model/__value                      # "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"
89	│   │   │   └── provider/__value                   # "anthropic"
90	│   │   ├── entire/
91	│   │   │   ├── token-usage/
92	│   │   │   │   ├── input/__value
93	│   │   │   │   ├── output/__value
94	│   │   │   │   ├── cache-read/__value
95	│   │   │   │   ├── cache-creation/__value
96	│   │   │   │   ├── api-calls/__value
97	│   │   │   │   └── total/__value
98	│   │   │   └── attribution/
99	│   │   │       ├── calculated-at/__value
100	│   │   │       ├── agent-lines/__value
101	│   │   │       ├── agent-removed/__value
102	│   │   │       ├── human-added/__value
103	│   │   │       ├── human-modified/__value
104	│   │   │       ├── human-removed/__value
105	│   │   │       ├── total-committed/__value
106	│   │   │       ├── total-lines-changed/__value
107	│   │   │       ├── agent-percentage/__value
108	│   │   │       └── metric-version/__value
109	│   │   ├── prompt/__value                         # user prompt(s)
110	│   │   └── transcript/__list/                     # chunked JSONL entries
111	│   │       ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
112	│   │       └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
113	│   └── <session-id-2>/
114	│       ├── agent/
115	│       │   ├── name/__value
116	│       │   ├── model/__value
117	│       │   └── provider/__value
118	│       ├── prompt/__value
119	│       └── transcript/__list/
120	│           └── ...
121	```
122	
123	This means:
124	- Checkpoint-level fields (`strategy`, `branch`, `files-touched`) live at the top level
125	- Each session gets its own subtree under `session/<session-id>/`
126	- `session/ids` is a list preserving session ordering
127	- Adding a session (via `entire attach` or concurrent agent) appends to `session/ids` and creates a new `session/<id>/` subtree — no overwrites
128	- Entire-specific structured metrics live under `session/<id>/entire/...` so they stay queryable without pretending to be standard gmeta keys
129	
130	### Single-Session Shorthand
131	
132	When there is exactly one session, the layout is identical — just one `session/<id>/` subtree. No special-casing needed.
133	
134	## Security: Redaction
135	
136	All data written to `refs/meta/local/main` MUST be redacted before creating git blobs, matching v1/v2 behavior:
137	
138	- Transcripts: pass through `redact.JSONLBytes()` before chunking into list entries
139	- Prompts: pass through `redact.String()` before writing `__value` blob
140	- File paths in `files-touched`: no redaction needed (already public via git history)
141	
142	This is a hard requirement, not an implementation detail. The gmeta ref is permanent and pushable.
143	
144	## Write Paths
145	
146	`GmetaStore` must be wired into **all** paths that write committed checkpoints, not just condensation:
147	
148	| Write path | File | When | Task checkpoints |
149	|---|---|---|---|
150	| Condensation | `manual_commit_condensation.go` | PostCommit hook — session data condensed on user commit | Full support |
151	| Stop finalization | `manual_commit_hooks.go` | Stop hook — transcript/prompts replaced with final versions | Full support |
152	| Attach | `attach.go` | `entire attach` — adds external session data to existing checkpoint | Full support |
153	| Migrate | `migrate.go` | `entire migrate` — copies v1 checkpoints to v2 (and now gmeta) | **Session data only** |
154	
155	**Migrate and task checkpoints**: Migration copies task metadata from v1 to v2 via raw tree splicing (`copyTaskMetadataToV2`), not through `WriteCommittedOptions` — the opts only carry `IsTask` and `ToolUseID`, not `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, subagent transcript content, or incremental payloads. Building a v1-tree-walker that re-extracts all task fields into gmeta format is not worth the complexity for a one-time operation. The gmeta migrate path writes session-level data only; task metadata remains available in v1 and v2.
156	
157	### Task Checkpoint Encoding
158	
159	Task checkpoints (subagent work) are written under `session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`:
160	
161	```
162	session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/
163	├── agent-id/__value                              # subagent identifier (opts.AgentID)
164	├── checkpoint-uuid/__value                       # UUID for transcript truncation on rewind (opts.CheckpointUUID)
165	├── transcript/__list/                            # subagent transcript (chunked, from opts.SubagentTranscriptPath)
166	│   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
167	│   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
168	└── incremental/__list/                           # incremental checkpoints (ordered)
169	    ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                       # JSON: {type, tool_use_id, data}
170	    └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
171	```
172	
173	These fields map 1:1 to what `WriteCommittedOptions` already carries: `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, `SubagentTranscriptPath`, and `IncrementalData`/`IncrementalType`/`IncrementalSequence`. No new plumbing needed.
174	
175	**Final task checkpoints** write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, and `transcript` entries.
176	
177	**Incremental task checkpoints** (`opts.IsIncremental`) append to `incremental/__list/`. Each entry is a JSON blob with `{type, tool_use_id, timestamp, data}` — same content as v1's `checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json` but as a gmeta list entry instead of numbered files.
178	
179	Redaction applies to both: subagent transcripts via `redact.JSONLBytes()` (falling back to `redact.Bytes()`), incremental data via `redact.JSONLBytes()`.
180	
181	### Task Key Policy
182	
183	Task checkpoint keys are **Entire-specific gmeta data**. They are intentionally
184	serialized in the gmeta exchange tree so they can be transported and materialized
185	by generic gmeta tooling, but they are not expected to have any built-in
186	meaning to the Rust `gmeta` CLI beyond normal key/value storage.
187	
188	Decision for the POC:
189	- `session:<id>:task:<tool-use-id>:...` keys are treated as opaque vendor data
190	- The Rust `gmeta` CLI only needs to preserve and expose them via normal
191	  `get`/`inspect` behavior
192	- Entire remains responsible for interpreting `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`,
193	  `transcript`, and `incremental` semantics
194	
195	Examples:
196	
197	```bash
198	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:agent-id
199	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:checkpoint-uuid
200	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:transcript
201	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:incremental
202	```
203	
204	This keeps the exchange format interoperable without requiring the Rust CLI to
205	understand Entire's subagent/task model.
206	
207	### Entire Metrics Schema
208	
209	Token usage and attribution are Entire-specific, so they are namespaced under
210	`session/<session-id>/entire/` rather than mixed into the generic session keys.
211	This keeps them queryable via gmeta while making it explicit that they are
212	vendor-defined fields, not part of the base spec.
213	
214	**Token usage** is stored as individual scalar values under
215	`session/<session-id>/entire/token-usage/`:
216	
217	```
218	session/<session-id>/entire/token-usage/
219	├── input/__value
220	├── output/__value
221	├── cache-read/__value
222	├── cache-creation/__value
223	├── api-calls/__value
224	└── total/__value
225	```
226	
227	These map directly to `agent.TokenUsage`. Storing them as separate values keeps
228	them easy to query with `gmeta get change-id:<id> session:<sid>:entire:token-usage:input`.
229	
230	**Attribution** is stored as individual scalar values under
231	`session/<session-id>/entire/attribution/`:
232	
233	```
234	session/<session-id>/entire/attribution/
235	├── calculated-at/__value
236	├── agent-lines/__value
237	├── agent-removed/__value
238	├── human-added/__value
239	├── human-modified/__value
240	├── human-removed/__value
241	├── total-committed/__value
242	├── total-lines-changed/__value
243	├── agent-percentage/__value
244	└── metric-version/__value
245	```
246	
247	These map directly to `checkpoint.InitialAttribution`.
248	
249	**Checkpoint-level combined attribution** is stored at `entire/combined-attribution/`
250	using the same scalar field names as session attribution. This maps directly to
251	`checkpoint.CheckpointSummary.CombinedAttribution` and is updated after the full
252	set of sessions for a checkpoint is known.
253	
254	Decision for the POC:
255	- Token usage is written and read at the session level
256	- Attribution is written and read at the session level
257	- Combined attribution is written and read at the checkpoint level
258	
259	### Write API
260	
261	```go
262	type GmetaStore struct {
263	    repo *git.Repository
264	    gs   *GitStore
265	}
266	
267	// WriteCommitted writes or appends a session to a checkpoint in gmeta format.
268	// If the checkpoint already exists, the new session is added alongside existing ones.
269	// Handles both session and task checkpoints (including incremental).
270	func (s *GmetaStore) WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error
271	
272	// UpdateCommitted replaces transcript and prompts for an existing session.
273	// Used at stop time to finalize with complete session data.
274	// Replaces the transcript list entries and prompt value for the given session.
275	func (s *GmetaStore) UpdateCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts UpdateCommittedOptions) error
276	```
277	
278	Both methods required from day one. `UpdateCommitted` replaces the `session/<id>/transcript/__list/` entries and `session/<id>/prompt/__value` blob for the target session. This matches the replace semantics v1/v2 already use — gmeta lists are append-only in the *exchange* model, but within a single serialization we control the full tree, so replacing entries before push is fine.
279	
280	### Wiring Pattern
281	
282	Same as v2 — non-fatal wrapper so gmeta failures don't break existing flow:
283	
284	```go
285	gmetaStore := cpkg.NewGmetaStore(repo)
286	if err := gmetaStore.WriteCommitted(ctx, opts); err != nil {
287	    logging.Warn(ctx, "gmeta write failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
288	}
289	```
290	
291	Applied in all four write paths above.
292	
293	## Steps
294	
295	### Step 1: GmetaStore struct + WriteCommitted + UpdateCommitted
296	
297	New file: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go`
298	
299	Implementation details:
300	- String values: blob at `<key-path>/__value`
301	- List values: blobs at `<key-path>/__list/<timestamp-ms>-<hash5>`
302	- Set values: blobs at `<key-path>/__set/<sha1-of-value[:10]>` containing the value
303	- Target base path: `change-id/<sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]>/<checkpoint-id>/`
304	- Ref: `refs/meta/local/main`
305	- Redaction: `redact.JSONLBytes()` for transcripts, `redact.String()` for prompts
306	- Multi-session: read existing tree, find/create `session/<id>/` subtree
307	
308	Reuses from `GitStore`: `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit`
309	
310	### Step 2: Wire into all write paths
311	
312	Add `GmetaStore` calls to condensation, stop finalization, attach, and migrate. Non-fatal in all paths.
313	
314	### Step 3: Validate interop
315	
316	Install the Rust gmeta CLI, point at a repo with Entire checkpoints:
317	
318	```bash
319	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:agent:model
320	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:prompt
321	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:transcript
322	gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> entire:files-touched
323	```
324	
325	Verify data round-trips correctly.
326	
327	## Open Questions
328	
329	- **Push/fetch**: gmeta uses `refs/meta/local/main` for push, `refs/meta/remotes/main` for fetch. Need to decide if this coexists with or replaces v2's push mechanism. Likely coexists for now.
330	- **Read-side**: Not needed for POC. Future work to have `entire session list/show` read from gmeta format.
331	
332	## Estimated Scope
333	
334	~300-400 lines for `GmetaStore` (write + update + multi-session handling + redaction), ~20 lines to wire into all four write paths. Tests + interop validation on top.

Spec: `gmeta/spec/README.md`

## Goal

Write Entire checkpoint metadata in gmeta exchange format alongside v1/v2, proving interop by reading it back with the Rust `gmeta` CLI.

## Coexistence Policy

For the current rollout, `v2` and `gmeta` are allowed to coexist, but only as
an explicit opt-in via separate settings. There is no implicit dependency
between them.

- `strategy_options.checkpoints_v2 = true` enables v2 write/read/push behavior
- `strategy_options.gmeta = true` enables gmeta write/push behavior
- If both are true, parallel behavior is intentional and temporary
- `gmeta` does not require `checkpoints_v2`, and `checkpoints_v2` does not
  require `gmeta`
- Read precedence remains unchanged unless a future explicit setting is added
  (for example, `prefer_gmeta_reads`)

Operationally:
- `v2` remains the primary Entire-native storage format
- `gmeta` is an exchange/interoperability format written and pushed separately
- gmeta fetch/materialize is independent of v2 fetch logic
- gmeta failures must remain non-fatal to the v1/v2 checkpoint flow
- Current fallback reads from `gmeta` are compatibility behavior, not backend
  selection policy. They exist to keep resume/log lookup working while the
  rollout is in progress and should not be treated as a stable precedence model.

## Architecture

No go-git changes needed. gmeta is just a tree layout convention — Entire already has all the plumbing:
- `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit` in `checkpoint/`
- `V2GitStore` as prior art for a second store struct composing `GitStore`
- Dual-write pattern already exists in `manual_commit_condensation.go`

## Tree Layout Mapping

### Fanout Rule

Per gmeta spec (`spec/exchange-format/exchange.md`), `change-id` targets use: **first 2 hex chars of SHA-1(target-value)**.

So for checkpoint ID `a3b2c4d5e6f7`: fanout = `sha1("a3b2c4d5e6f7")[:2]`.

This is NOT the same as `checkpoint-id[:2]`. The fanout is derived from a hash of the value, not the value itself.

### Per-Session Encoding

A checkpoint can contain multiple sessions (concurrent agents, `entire attach`). gmeta has no native session concept, so we namespace per session under the checkpoint's change-id target:

```
change-id/<fanout>/<checkpoint-id>/
├── entire/
│   ├── strategy/__value                           # "manual-commit"
│   ├── cli-version/__value                        # CLI version
│   ├── branch/__value                             # branch name
│   ├── checkpoints-count/__value                  # total across all sessions
│   ├── combined-attribution/
│   │   ├── calculated-at/__value
│   │   ├── agent-lines/__value
│   │   ├── agent-removed/__value
│   │   ├── human-added/__value
│   │   ├── human-modified/__value
│   │   ├── human-removed/__value
│   │   ├── total-committed/__value
│   │   ├── total-lines-changed/__value
│   │   ├── agent-percentage/__value
│   │   └── metric-version/__value
│   └── files-touched/__set/                       # merged from all sessions
│       ├── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/foo.go"
│       └── <sha1(value)[:10]>                     # "src/bar.go"
├── session/
│   ├── ids/__list/                                # ordered session IDs
│   │   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid1"
│   │   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>                    # "2026-01-13-uuid2"
│   ├── <session-id-1>/
│   │   ├── agent/
│   │   │   ├── name/__value                       # "Claude Code"
│   │   │   ├── model/__value                      # "claude-opus-4-6[1m]"
│   │   │   └── provider/__value                   # "anthropic"
│   │   ├── entire/
│   │   │   ├── token-usage/
│   │   │   │   ├── input/__value
│   │   │   │   ├── output/__value
│   │   │   │   ├── cache-read/__value
│   │   │   │   ├── cache-creation/__value
│   │   │   │   ├── api-calls/__value
│   │   │   │   └── total/__value
│   │   │   └── attribution/
│   │   │       ├── calculated-at/__value
│   │   │       ├── agent-lines/__value
│   │   │       ├── agent-removed/__value
│   │   │       ├── human-added/__value
│   │   │       ├── human-modified/__value
│   │   │       ├── human-removed/__value
│   │   │       ├── total-committed/__value
│   │   │       ├── total-lines-changed/__value
│   │   │       ├── agent-percentage/__value
│   │   │       └── metric-version/__value
│   │   ├── prompt/__value                         # user prompt(s)
│   │   └── transcript/__list/                     # chunked JSONL entries
│   │       ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   │       └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   └── <session-id-2>/
│       ├── agent/
│       │   ├── name/__value
│       │   ├── model/__value
│       │   └── provider/__value
│       ├── prompt/__value
│       └── transcript/__list/
│           └── ...
```

This means:
- Checkpoint-level fields (`strategy`, `branch`, `files-touched`) live at the top level
- Each session gets its own subtree under `session/<session-id>/`
- `session/ids` is a list preserving session ordering
- Adding a session (via `entire attach` or concurrent agent) appends to `session/ids` and creates a new `session/<id>/` subtree — no overwrites
- Entire-specific structured metrics live under `session/<id>/entire/...` so they stay queryable without pretending to be standard gmeta keys

### Single-Session Shorthand

When there is exactly one session, the layout is identical — just one `session/<id>/` subtree. No special-casing needed.

## Security: Redaction

All data written to `refs/meta/local/main` MUST be redacted before creating git blobs, matching v1/v2 behavior:

- Transcripts: pass through `redact.JSONLBytes()` before chunking into list entries
- Prompts: pass through `redact.String()` before writing `__value` blob
- File paths in `files-touched`: no redaction needed (already public via git history)

This is a hard requirement, not an implementation detail. The gmeta ref is permanent and pushable.

## Write Paths

`GmetaStore` must be wired into **all** paths that write committed checkpoints, not just condensation:

| Write path | File | When | Task checkpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| Condensation | `manual_commit_condensation.go` | PostCommit hook — session data condensed on user commit | Full support |
| Stop finalization | `manual_commit_hooks.go` | Stop hook — transcript/prompts replaced with final versions | Full support |
| Attach | `attach.go` | `entire attach` — adds external session data to existing checkpoint | Full support |
| Migrate | `migrate.go` | `entire migrate` — copies v1 checkpoints to v2 (and now gmeta) | **Session data only** |

**Migrate and task checkpoints**: Migration copies task metadata from v1 to v2 via raw tree splicing (`copyTaskMetadataToV2`), not through `WriteCommittedOptions` — the opts only carry `IsTask` and `ToolUseID`, not `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, subagent transcript content, or incremental payloads. Building a v1-tree-walker that re-extracts all task fields into gmeta format is not worth the complexity for a one-time operation. The gmeta migrate path writes session-level data only; task metadata remains available in v1 and v2.

### Task Checkpoint Encoding

Task checkpoints (subagent work) are written under `session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/`:

```
session/<session-id>/task/<tool-use-id>/
├── agent-id/__value                              # subagent identifier (opts.AgentID)
├── checkpoint-uuid/__value                       # UUID for transcript truncation on rewind (opts.CheckpointUUID)
├── transcript/__list/                            # subagent transcript (chunked, from opts.SubagentTranscriptPath)
│   ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>
│   └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
└── incremental/__list/                           # incremental checkpoints (ordered)
    ├── <timestamp>-<hash5>                       # JSON: {type, tool_use_id, data}
    └── <timestamp>-<hash5>
```

These fields map 1:1 to what `WriteCommittedOptions` already carries: `AgentID`, `CheckpointUUID`, `SubagentTranscriptPath`, and `IncrementalData`/`IncrementalType`/`IncrementalSequence`. No new plumbing needed.

**Final task checkpoints** write `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`, and `transcript` entries.

**Incremental task checkpoints** (`opts.IsIncremental`) append to `incremental/__list/`. Each entry is a JSON blob with `{type, tool_use_id, timestamp, data}` — same content as v1's `checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json` but as a gmeta list entry instead of numbered files.

Redaction applies to both: subagent transcripts via `redact.JSONLBytes()` (falling back to `redact.Bytes()`), incremental data via `redact.JSONLBytes()`.

### Task Key Policy

Task checkpoint keys are **Entire-specific gmeta data**. They are intentionally
serialized in the gmeta exchange tree so they can be transported and materialized
by generic gmeta tooling, but they are not expected to have any built-in
meaning to the Rust `gmeta` CLI beyond normal key/value storage.

Decision for the POC:
- `session:<id>:task:<tool-use-id>:...` keys are treated as opaque vendor data
- The Rust `gmeta` CLI only needs to preserve and expose them via normal
  `get`/`inspect` behavior
- Entire remains responsible for interpreting `agent-id`, `checkpoint-uuid`,
  `transcript`, and `incremental` semantics

Examples:

```bash
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:agent-id
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:checkpoint-uuid
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:transcript
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:task:<tool-use-id>:incremental
```

This keeps the exchange format interoperable without requiring the Rust CLI to
understand Entire's subagent/task model.

### Entire Metrics Schema

Token usage and attribution are Entire-specific, so they are namespaced under
`session/<session-id>/entire/` rather than mixed into the generic session keys.
This keeps them queryable via gmeta while making it explicit that they are
vendor-defined fields, not part of the base spec.

**Token usage** is stored as individual scalar values under
`session/<session-id>/entire/token-usage/`:

```
session/<session-id>/entire/token-usage/
├── input/__value
├── output/__value
├── cache-read/__value
├── cache-creation/__value
├── api-calls/__value
└── total/__value
```

These map directly to `agent.TokenUsage`. Storing them as separate values keeps
them easy to query with `gmeta get change-id:<id> session:<sid>:entire:token-usage:input`.

**Attribution** is stored as individual scalar values under
`session/<session-id>/entire/attribution/`:

```
session/<session-id>/entire/attribution/
├── calculated-at/__value
├── agent-lines/__value
├── agent-removed/__value
├── human-added/__value
├── human-modified/__value
├── human-removed/__value
├── total-committed/__value
├── total-lines-changed/__value
├── agent-percentage/__value
└── metric-version/__value
```

These map directly to `checkpoint.InitialAttribution`.

**Checkpoint-level combined attribution** is stored at `entire/combined-attribution/`
using the same scalar field names as session attribution. This maps directly to
`checkpoint.CheckpointSummary.CombinedAttribution` and is updated after the full
set of sessions for a checkpoint is known.

Decision for the POC:
- Token usage is written and read at the session level
- Attribution is written and read at the session level
- Combined attribution is written and read at the checkpoint level

### Write API

```go
type GmetaStore struct {
    repo *git.Repository
    gs   *GitStore
}

// WriteCommitted writes or appends a session to a checkpoint in gmeta format.
// If the checkpoint already exists, the new session is added alongside existing ones.
// Handles both session and task checkpoints (including incremental).
func (s *GmetaStore) WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error

// UpdateCommitted replaces transcript and prompts for an existing session.
// Used at stop time to finalize with complete session data.
// Replaces the transcript list entries and prompt value for the given session.
func (s *GmetaStore) UpdateCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts UpdateCommittedOptions) error
```

Both methods required from day one. `UpdateCommitted` replaces the `session/<id>/transcript/__list/` entries and `session/<id>/prompt/__value` blob for the target session. This matches the replace semantics v1/v2 already use — gmeta lists are append-only in the *exchange* model, but within a single serialization we control the full tree, so replacing entries before push is fine.

### Wiring Pattern

Same as v2 — non-fatal wrapper so gmeta failures don't break existing flow:

```go
gmetaStore := cpkg.NewGmetaStore(repo)
if err := gmetaStore.WriteCommitted(ctx, opts); err != nil {
    logging.Warn(ctx, "gmeta write failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
}
```

Applied in all four write paths above.

## Steps

### Step 1: GmetaStore struct + WriteCommitted + UpdateCommitted

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go`

Implementation details:
- String values: blob at `<key-path>/__value`
- List values: blobs at `<key-path>/__list/<timestamp-ms>-<hash5>`
- Set values: blobs at `<key-path>/__set/<sha1-of-value[:10]>` containing the value
- Target base path: `change-id/<sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]>/<checkpoint-id>/`
- Ref: `refs/meta/local/main`
- Redaction: `redact.JSONLBytes()` for transcripts, `redact.String()` for prompts
- Multi-session: read existing tree, find/create `session/<id>/` subtree

Reuses from `GitStore`: `BuildTreeFromEntries`, `CreateBlobFromContent`, `CreateCommit`

### Step 2: Wire into all write paths

Add `GmetaStore` calls to condensation, stop finalization, attach, and migrate. Non-fatal in all paths.

### Step 3: Validate interop

Install the Rust gmeta CLI, point at a repo with Entire checkpoints:

```bash
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:agent:model
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:prompt
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> session:<session-id>:transcript
gmeta get change-id:<checkpoint-id> entire:files-touched
```

Verify data round-trips correctly.

## Open Questions

- **Push/fetch**: gmeta uses `refs/meta/local/main` for push, `refs/meta/remotes/main` for fetch. Need to decide if this coexists with or replaces v2's push mechanism. Likely coexists for now.
- **Read-side**: Not needed for POC. Future work to have `entire session list/show` read from gmeta format.

## Estimated Scope

~300-400 lines for `GmetaStore` (write + update + multi-session handling + redaction), ~20 lines to wire into all four write paths. Tests + interop validation on top.

## Thorough Comparison of v1/v2 vs gmeta Checkpoint Storage Models

Based on my analysis of the codebase, here's a detailed structural comparison:

---

### 1. **Ref Structure**

**v1:**
- Single ref: `entire/checkpoints/v1` (orphan branch)
- All metadata (prompts, transcripts, session info, checksums) stored on this one branch
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go:43`

**v2:**
- Two refs:
  - `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/main` (stores permanent metadata + compact transcripts)
  - `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current` (stores raw/full transcripts)
  - Plus archived generation refs: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<0000000000001>` etc.
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go:49-58`
- v2 uses custom refs under `refs/entire/` (invisible in GitHub UI, not fetched by default)

**gmeta:**
- Single ref: `refs/meta/local/main` (gmeta exchange format)
- Remote ref mapping: `refs/meta/main` (no `local/` prefix on remote)
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:31-38`

**Key difference:** v2 splits persistent metadata from large raw transcripts across two refs; gmeta uses one ref. v2 supports generation rotation; gmeta does not.

---

### 2. **Identifier Mapping (Sharding)**

**v1/v2:**
- Path: `checkpoint-id[:2]/checkpoint-id[2:]`
- Example: `a3b2c4d5e6f7` → `a3/b2c4d5e6f7`
- Uses first 2 characters of checkpoint ID as shard directory
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id/id.go:83-88`

**gmeta:**
- Path: `change-id/sha1(checkpoint-id)[:2]/checkpoint-id`
- Uses `gmetaFanout()` which computes `SHA-1(checkpoint-id)[:2]` for the shard
- Example: `a3b2c4d5e6f7` → `change-id/XY/a3b2c4d5e6f7` (where XY is first 2 hex chars of SHA-1)
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:169-179`

**Key difference:** gmeta uses SHA-1 hash-based fanout (more uniform distribution), while v1/v2 uses direct ID prefix (simpler, lexicographic grouping). gmeta adds `change-id/` prefix per gmeta spec.

---

### 3. **Session Indexing**

**v1/v2:**
- Integer-indexed subdirectories: `0/`, `1/`, `2/`, etc.
- Sessions stored sequentially by index
- First session at `<checkpoint-id>/0/`, second at `<checkpoint-id>/1/`, etc.
- Session lookup requires finding the index by ID
- Enables O(1) random access to nth session if index is known
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:290-312`

**gmeta:**
- Named session ID keys: `session/<session-id>/`
- Session IDs used directly as directory names (not indices)
- Multi-session ordering: `session/ids/__list/` maintains append order using timestamp-based list entries
- Lookup is O(n) to find a session ID, but order preserved via list metadata
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:86-87, 526-563`

**Key difference:** v1/v2 use integer indices for direct access; gmeta uses named keys with explicit ordering metadata. gmeta preserves order even across edits via timestamped list entries.

---

### 4. **Transcript Storage**

**v1:**
- Single file: `full.jsonl`
- Optionally chunked if large: `full.jsonl.001`, `full.jsonl.002`, etc.
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go:30-31`
- Stored at session level: `<checkpoint-id>/<session-index>/full.jsonl`

**v2:**
- **On `/main` ref:** Compact transcript: `transcript.jsonl`
- **On `/full/current` ref:** Raw transcript: `raw_transcript` (chunked: `raw_transcript.001`, etc.)
- Dual-write strategy: metadata on main, raw data on full/current
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go:32-35`
- Stored per-session: `<checkpoint-id>/<session-index>/transcript.jsonl` (main) and `raw_transcript` (full)

**gmeta:**
- **Chunked into list entries:** `session/<session-id>/transcript/__list/<timestamp>-<hash-prefix>`
- Each chunk stored as individual blob under `transcript/__list/`
- Concatenated on read via `readGmetaListConcat()`
- Chunks ordered by embedded timestamp for deterministic reassembly
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:496-524, 1096-1125`

**Implications:**
- v1/v2: Simple file-based, easy to read entire transcript in one operation
- gmeta: List-based chunks enable more granular updates and gmeta spec compliance; requires concatenation on read

---

### 5. **Metadata Format**

**v1/v2:**
- JSON metadata files: `metadata.json` (per-session), checkpoint summary
- One metadata file per session: `<checkpoint-id>/<session-index>/metadata.json`
- Root checkpoint summary: `<checkpoint-id>/metadata.json`
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go:36`

**gmeta:**
- Individual `__value` files for each field:
  - `entire/strategy/__value`
  - `entire/cli-version/__value`
  - `agent/name/__value`
  - `agent/model/__value`
  - `entire/token-usage/input/__value`, `output/__value`, etc.
  - `entire/attribution/agent-lines/__value`, etc.
- Set values stored as `__set/` entries (one file per set member)
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:196-223, 565-576`

**Implications:**
- v1/v2: Single read of `metadata.json` gives all session data
- gmeta: Multiple reads required (one per field), but individual fields queryable via gmeta set/string value API; fields stored as separate `__value` files for granular access

---

### 6. **Generation/Rotation**

**v1:**
- No generation system
- Single linear history on `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch
- Indefinite growth of single ref

**v2:**
- **Generation system with automatic rotation:**
  - Current generation: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/current`
  - Archived generations: `refs/entire/checkpoints/v2/full/<13-digit-number>` (e.g., `full/0000000000001`)
  - Rotation threshold: `DefaultMaxCheckpointsPerGeneration = 100`
  - When /full/current reaches 100 checkpoints, it's archived with `generation.json` metadata
  - New empty /full/current created for next 100 checkpoints
- Generation metadata: `generation.json` (written to tree root at archive time only)
- Tracks `OldestCheckpointAt` and `NewestCheckpointAt` timestamps
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_generation.go:24-27, 152-189`

**gmeta:**
- No generation/rotation system
- Single ref grows indefinitely like v1
- No built-in archival mechanism

**Key difference:** v2 proactively manages ref growth via generation rotation; gmeta and v1 do not.

---

### 7. **Temporary Checkpoints (Shadow Branches)**

**v1/v2:**
- Both use shadow branches for per-step checkpoints during development
- Shadow branch naming: `entire/<7-char-base-commit-hash>-<6-char-worktree-hash>`
- Example: `entire/a3b2c4d-abc123`
- One shadow branch per worktree per base commit
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/temporary.go:34-69`
- Written with `WriteTemporary()`; deduplication via tree hash comparison (line 120)
- Shadow branches are regular git branches (not under refs/entire/)

**gmeta:**
- Does NOT appear to have an equivalent shadow branch system
- No `WriteTemporary()` equivalent in gmeta_store.go
- Gmeta store only has `WriteCommitted()` and `UpdateCommitted()`

**Implications:**
- v1/v2 support work-in-progress persistence per step
- gmeta only supports committed checkpoints; no per-step temporary storage

---

### 8. **Commit History**

**v1:**
- One commit per condensation on the metadata branch
- Commit message format: `Checkpoint: <id>` with trailers (Session, Strategy, Agent, etc.)
- Trailers include: `Session:`, `Strategy:`, `Agent:`, `Ephemeral-Branch:`, `Metadata-Task:`
- Linear history (each checkpoint adds one commit)
- Located in `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:810-835`

**v2:**
- Commits on TWO refs:
  - `/main`: one commit per session write (metadata + compact transcript)
  - `/full/current`: one commit per session write (raw transcript only)
  - Archived generation refs: inherit history from /full/current, don't get new commits

Here's my synthesis of what differs and what would break if you switched from v1/v2 to gmeta-only:

## Key Architectural Differences

| | v1/v2 | gmeta |
|---|---|---|
| **Refs** | 3+ refs (v1 branch, v2/main, v2/full/current, archived generations) | 1 ref (`refs/meta/local/main`) |
| **Sharding** | `id[:2]/id[2:]` (direct prefix) | `sha1(id)[:2]/id` (hash-based fanout per gmeta spec) |
| **Sessions** | Integer-indexed (`0/`, `1/`, `2/`) | Named by session ID directly |
| **Transcripts** | Single files (`full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl`) | Chunked into `__list/` entries, reassembled on read |
| **Metadata** | One `metadata.json` per session | One `__value` file per field |
| **Rotation** | v2 archives generations at 100 checkpoints | None — single ref grows forever |
| **Temporary checkpoints** | Shadow branches (`entire/<hash>-<worktree>`) | Not supported |

## What Would Break or Need Work to Switch

### 1. No temporary checkpoints (shadow branches)
This is the biggest gap. The entire rewind system (`entire rewind`) depends on shadow branches storing per-step snapshots of working tree state. gmeta has no equivalent — it only writes on commit. You'd need to either:
- Keep shadow branches as-is (they're orthogonal to committed storage)
- Or build a gmeta equivalent for per-step data, which the spec doesn't naturally support

**Discussed in conversations:** Intentionally scoped out — "gmeta writes only on PostCommit when sessions condense." Shadow branches would likely stay regardless.

### 2. No generation rotation — ref growth is unbounded
v2 archives refs at 100 checkpoints to keep individual ref sizes manageable. gmeta has nothing like this. Over months of use, `refs/meta/local/main` would accumulate every checkpoint's full transcript data on a single ref. This affects:
- Clone/fetch performance (one giant ref)
- Git object store bloat on the remote

**Not discussed in conversations** — this is a gap that wasn't surfaced during the POC.

### 3. Transcript chunking changes read patterns
v1/v2 read a transcript as one file. gmeta requires reading N list entries and concatenating. The `readGmetaListConcat` function handles this, but it's inherently more I/O (multiple tree lookups per transcript). For large transcripts, this could matter.

**Discussed in conversations:** The interop session found that the Rust `gmeta` CLI handled chunked transcripts correctly, but performance wasn't tested at scale.

### 4. Metadata granularity is inverted
v1/v2: one `metadata.json` read gives you everything about a session. gmeta: you need to walk the tree and read individual `__value` blobs for each field. `ReadCommitted` in gmeta already does this, but it's ~20 tree lookups vs 1 file read.

**Discussed in conversations:** This was a deliberate design choice — individual keys are queryable via `gmeta get`, which is the whole point of the exchange format. But it's a read performance tradeoff.

### 5. Different fanout means no shared lookup path
v1/v2 shard by `id[:2]`, gmeta shards by `sha1(id)[:2]`. You can't look up the same checkpoint with the same path on both stores. Any code that assumes a specific tree layout needs to know which store it's talking to. This is already handled by having separate store types, but it means you can't unify the tree structures.

**Discussed in conversations:** Noted in the plan as a gmeta spec requirement. The fanout difference is inherent to the gmeta spec's design for uniform distribution.

### 6. Session ordering uses different mechanisms
v1/v2 rely on integer indices and a `session_ids` array in `metadata.json`. gmeta uses a `session/ids/__list/` with timestamp-prefixed entry names. The ordering bug (fixed in `20a5b2cbdeb5`) showed this is fragile — lexicographic sort of list entries doesn't match insertion order without the timestamp prefix.

**Discussed in conversations:** Found during code review. Fixed by using monotonic timestamp prefixes in list entry IDs. But this means ordering correctness depends on clock monotonicity, which integer indices don't.

### 7. Read-side integration is minimal
Only `resume.go` uses gmeta as a fallback read source. The explain, session list, session show, and status commands all read from v1/v2 only. Switching would require wiring gmeta reads into every command that consumes checkpoint data.

**Discussed in conversations:** Explicitly deferred as "future work" in the plan. The conversations noted: "read precedence remains unchanged unless a future explicit setting is added."

### 8. Migration doesn't carry combined attribution
The `entire migrate --checkpoints gmeta` path writes session data but doesn't call `UpdateCheckpointSummary` for combined attribution. So migrated checkpoints would be missing their aggregated stats.

**Discussed in conversations:** Noted in the migration session (`ba2e77f6daf4`) — the user asked "would migrate work now?" and the review flagged this gap, but it wasn't fixed.

### 9. Push works, fetch doesn't exist
gmeta pushes `refs/meta/local/main:refs/meta/main`, but there's no fetch/materialization on the receiving side. A collaborator who pulls your repo wouldn't get your gmeta data without manual ref fetching.

**Discussed in conversations:** Explicitly deferred. The plan says "gmeta fetch/materialize is independent of v2 fetch logic" but no implementation exists.

## Bottom Line

The gmeta format works well as an **exchange layer** — it writes the same data in a spec-compliant format that external tools (Rust `gmeta` CLI) can read. But as a **primary storage backend**, it's missing three things v2 has: temporary checkpoints (rewind), generation rotation (scalability), and comprehensive read integration (commands). The conversations consistently treated gmeta as "alongside, not instead of" v1/v2, and the coexistence policy in the plan doc makes that explicit.
